textContent.text: Imagine you are in the audience of a circus. A herd of golden horses gallops around the ring. You gasp, flabbergasted, as a giant orange goldfish swishes its fins in midair. Suddenly, a twenty-foot-tall elephant doing a handstand appears in the ring! It sounds unbelievable, but it's just another show at Circus Roncalli. Unlike traditional circuses that use live animals, this German circus uses technology to create holograms, or projected 3D pictures, of animals.

Why holograms? First, it is expensive to transport and care for live animals, especially large ones like elephants. One elephant can weigh more than three pickup trucks and can eat more than two hundred pounds of food per day! But a holographic elephant is weightless and does not require food. Second, the place where the circus performs has changed over time. Circus Roncalli used to perform outside of cities in large meadows. This gave them lots of space for their animals. Now, Circus Roncalli performs in busy cities. They set up in small parking lots that have little room for large animals. Third, circus life is hard work for animals. Switching to holographs helps Circus Roncalli avoid harming animals.

Using a hologram is convenient, but making a hologram is not an easy task. First, engineers use computers to show a 3D model of the animal. Then, the engineers determine how audience members will see the animal from every seat. When the hologram is finished, the image is projected in the circus ring for the audience to enjoy. To create one holographic elephant, Circus Roncalli needs fifteen engineers, three thousand video processors, and eleven laser beams.

Even though there are not live animals, Circus Roncalli still entertains audiences with an exciting show. Audiences have fallen in love with the circus's delightful holograms. The animals may be imaginary, but the fun is definitely real!

textContent.text: Didgeridoos are long, slender wind instruments, ranging from three to ten feet in length. They consist of a hollow tube that the player blows through to make music. Didgeridoos are the traditional musical instruments of people native to northern Australia. The instruments are often used in ceremonies and for entertainment. For these reasons, the didgeridoo's deep, vibrating sound is often referred to as "the sound of Australia."

These instruments are traditionally made from bamboo or eucalyptus trees. Bamboo is already hollow, so bamboo instruments are easier to make. Eucalyptus instruments, however, take more work. First, termites hollow out sections of eucalyptus trees. Then, these sections are harvested and cleaned out. Finally, the outer bark is removed, and the instrument is ready to be played.

pieces.text: To play the didgeridoo, people vibrate their lips as they blow into the instrument. This produces a low humming sound. Some players can produce the sound for up to forty minutes without stopping! To do so, the players use

. When they start to run out of breath, they puff out their cheeks and hold the remaining air in their mouths. The players quickly breathe in through their noses while they expel air through their mouths to keep the sound going. The players use their tongues and cheeks to push the air out. Some players can also use their voices to create sounds resembling those of native Australian animals. For example, they can imitate the yelping of dingoes—Australian wild dogs—and the "laughing" of Australian birds called kookaburras.

textContent.text: Today, didgeridoos are also being made outside of Australia. People from around the world are making them from materials like glass, metal, and cactus. Modern musicians are blending the didgeridoo's earthy sounds into their own music. This links the sounds of today with the ancient, tribal sounds of native Australia.

textContent.text: Didgeridoos are long, slender wind instruments, ranging from three to ten feet in length. They consist of a hollow tube that the player blows through to make music. Didgeridoos are the traditional musical instruments of people native to northern Australia. The instruments are often used in ceremonies and for entertainment. For these reasons, the didgeridoo's deep, vibrating sound is often referred to as "the sound of Australia."

These instruments are traditionally made from bamboo or eucalyptus trees. Bamboo is already hollow, so bamboo instruments are easier to make. Eucalyptus instruments, however, take more work. First, termites hollow out sections of eucalyptus trees. Then, these sections are harvested and cleaned out. Finally, the outer bark is removed, and the instrument is ready to be played.

textContent.text: East Africa is home to the Maasai, a tribe of people living mainly in Kenya and Tanzania. The Maasai have been around for hundreds of years, and they still practice many ancient traditions. If you visit a traditional Maasai village today, you can learn about many of their customs.

pieces.text: One of the oldest Maasai customs is the ten-day ceremony called Eunoto. The purpose of this ritual is to show that a group of boys are ready to become men. During one part of the Eunoto ceremony, some Maasai boys have a chance to perform the
, a traditional jumping dance. The dance is reserved for Maasai boys who are
, or junior warriors in the tribe.

textContent.text: To prepare for the adumu, the boys dress in bright sheets of fabric. Red is the traditional color, so some will even dye their hair bright red to match. Many boys wear beads that will jingle as they move and dance. Some boys carry sticks to represent the spears of warriors. Once the boys are dressed, they are ready to begin the dance.

pieces.text: The word

means "jump" in the Maasai language, and that is exactly how the boys perform the dance. To begin, all the boys form a circle and take turns jumping in its center. When it is his turn to perform, a dancer will stand straight and jump with his feet together. He tries to go as high as possible. As the boy jumps, the other participants sing. The tones they sing depend on the height of the jumps. The higher the jump, the higher the boys sing. The dance is repeated over and over until each of the morani has had his turn in the circle.

textContent.text: While Nek Chand was growing up in India in the 1920s, he built forts and castles from objects he found around his village. He sculpted rock and clay figures to live in the buildings, too. Years later, Chand used his experience with building things out of unlikely materials to make his own city.

Starting in the 1950s, Chand worked as a road inspector. He began collecting rubble, such as broken pottery, rags, and tiles. To others, this was useless trash. To Chand, these were free materials he could use to create the city of his dreams. By the mid-1960s, with just a few simple tools, Chand used his rubble and concrete to create all sorts of buildings and figures. He secretly constructed his city at night in a secluded forest that belonged to the government. He did not want his creation to be discovered.

Chand's city grew bigger over time. He set up centers to collect larger amounts of trash from places across the city, such as hotels, restaurants, and hospitals. He turned the trash into sculptures of dancing women, monkeys, musicians, and more. Most of his figures are smaller than in real life. Some of the human sculptures have real hair that Chand collected from barber shops! He also made courtyards, waterfalls, and huge swings.

When Chand's city was finally discovered, people were amazed at his creativity and clever use of materials. In 1976, the city was officially recognized as a work of art and named the Rock Garden of Chandigarh. Today, it is a twenty-five-acre park with winding paths that lead to plazas and theaters. That's bigger than twenty football fields! India considers the garden a national treasure. The Rock Garden of Chandigarh still attracts over five thousand visitors from around the world who come to enjoy Chand's magical creation every day.

textContent.text: Under the first full moon of the year, music lovers in Norway huddle on ice benches covered with reindeer skins. On a frozen stage, musicians in furry hats and coats play instruments carved entirely from ice! This show is the Ice Music Festival, the only concert in the world of its kind. This cool idea began in 1999, when drummer Terje Isungset played music inside a frozen waterfall. The amazing sounds that he heard led him to start using ice as a musical instrument. Isungset spent years experimenting with ice instruments. The more he learned, the more excited he became. After years of experimenting, he founded the Ice Music Festival in 2016.

To prepare the frozen instruments, Isungset hunts for the best natural sources of ice. He tests each source of ice by cutting out a piece, tapping it with his finger, and listening to the sound it produces. Experience tells him whether the ice will make a good instrument. He prefers not to use human-made ice, because he claims frozen lake water sounds better. This claim may be supported by science. Scientists have noticed that natural ice has fewer bubbles, which could lead to a clearer sound.

Once the ice has been sourced, professional ice carvers use tools to create instruments. They carve everything from saxophones to xylophones. The carvers often change the look of the instruments, which causes creative or special sounds. Each year, the goal of the festival is to challenge musicians to make innovative music when playing these one-of-a-kind ice instruments.

Playing the frozen instruments is a challenge. Each performance surprises the musicians and the audience. After the concert is over, Isungset jokes that the musicians will drink their instruments. Actually, they just leave their stage and instruments behind, giving it all back to nature.

textContent.text: Weddings are celebrated in many different ways. The celebrations are full of traditions that have been passed down over time. In many cultures, guests traditionally give money as a wedding gift. Sometimes money is used as a part of the celebration. Other times, money is a symbol of good fortune to the new couple.

Different countries and cultures often have their own ways of giving money to couples. In Italy, a bride will often carry a bag for guests to place envelopes of money in. In China, guests usually put money inside a red envelope instead of a white one. This is supposed to bring the couple good fortune. Other cultures have more playful ways of giving money. For example, wedding guests in Cuba and Poland often pay to do a dance with the bride or groom. It is called the money dance. Often guests pin money on the couple's clothes as part of the fun. People in Nigeria also give the couple money while dancing. Guests throw money in the air, and it showers down on the bride and groom.

In some cultures, money is not just for gift giving. Coins can have special meanings when used in the wedding ceremony. For example, there is a custom in Sweden for the bride to put coins in her shoes. She places a silver coin from her father in her left shoe and a gold coin from her mother in her right shoe. The coins represent the parents' wish for the couple to have a good life. In Mexico, couples exchange thirteen gold coins during the ceremony. This shows that they agree to support one another.
Though these money traditions are different from culture to culture, they all share the same desire to convey love and support to a newly married couple.

, which means "little armored one" in Spanish, perfectly describes what the small animals look like. Armadillos look like rats that put on suits of armor! The head, body, and tail of armadillos are covered with scaly, leathery plates called
scutes

. Some people say that these scutes look like little interlocking shields. Others insist that the scutes look like pieces of armor that a knight would wear. But their strange appearance doesn't end there. While many animals have long legs and short noses, the armadillo has a long nose and short legs.

textSplitByBlanks.text: Winning the Triple Crown is the highest honor for a race horse. The Triple Crown goes to a horse that is able to win three major races back-to-back. This is quite difficult to achieve! The three Triple Crown races are called
jewels

. The first of the three jewels is the Kentucky Derby, which takes place every year in early May. The second jewel in the series, the Preakness Stakes, occurs two weeks later. Finally, the third jewel, the Belmont Stakes, takes place in June. Winning any of these horse races is a victory in its own right. However, winning one of these individual races is not nearly as difficult as winning all three jewels within the same year.

textSplitByBlanks.text: The small town of Dixville Notch, New Hampshire, has a population of roughly five people. It seems unlikely that a town this small would carry much weight in a U.S. election. However, Dixville Notch is home to a long-standing voting tradition in the United States. It is one of three tiny towns in New Hampshire that are first to vote for the next president. This is because Dixville Notch allows voting just after midnight on Election Day. So, the people of Dixville Notch usually stay up late to be the first voters in the nation. Of course, the outcome of the votes in this small town may not correctly predict the election winners. But these voters enjoy being among the first citizens to have their say.

They did so to see how the insects would be affected by traveling beyond the Earth's atmosphere. As the rocket came down, a capsule containing the fruit flies was carried back to Earth by parachute. textSplitByBlanks.text: Everything that happens to you is stored for a period of time as a memory. Your brain holds some memories for a long time and others for a short time. When something is stored in short-term memory, you're likely to forget it soon—usually in less than thirty seconds. Long-term memory, on the other hand, can last for years.

textSplitByBlanks.text: Some parts of your body perform tasks you can't see and help you in ways that may be surprising. The ear, in fact, has an important job besides allowing you to hear. It assists you with your balance. The inner ear is home to three tiny canals that have fluid and small hairs inside of them. The fluid and hairs perform the key duty of sensing the movement of your head. When you move your head, the fluid and small hairs also move. Then, the small hairs relay a message to your brain that your head is moving. After that, the brain sends a message to your muscles to help you stay balanced.

Many pizza chefs believe the best pizza pies are cooked in wood-fired brick ovens. And some scientists happen to agree with them. These scientists say that the wood fire along with the brick creates a high heat that transfers slowly. This allows the pizza crust and toppings to cook more evenly. Steel ovens, on the other hand, transfer heat quickly, causing pizza to cook unevenly. This means that the pizza crust might burn before the rest of the pizza has finished cooking.

textSplitByBlanks.text: What did you have to drink for breakfast this morning? If you answered "orange juice," then you are in good company. Since World War II, orange juice has been a popular drink in the United States. During World War II, the United States Army was looking for new ways to prevent a disease called
scurvy

. The best way to prevent scurvy is to eat fruits and vegetables high in vitamin C. However, sending fresh produce to soldiers in other countries was a challenge. These fruits and vegetables often spoiled before reaching the soldiers. To solve this problem, the U.S. government decided to send soldiers canned orange juice. The soldiers enjoyed this drink, and many continued to drink orange juice after they returned home.

textSplitByBlanks.text: Did you know that one of the longest animals in the world is a worm? In fact, it's a kind of ribbon worm called the bootlace worm, or the giant ribbon worm. Found off the northwest coast of the United Kingdom, the bootlace worm spends most of its life curled up like a tangled ball of yarn. Stretched out, the average length of a bootlace worm is 16 to 32 feet long. However, the longest bootlace worm ever found measured a whopping 180 feet long! Looking at it while it's coiled up, you might be fooled by its appearance. But don't let its curled-up size fool you.

textSplitByBlanks.text: How did the Canary Islands get their name? The name didn't come from the little yellow birds on the islands. In fact, the birds got their name from the islands, not the other way around. Though people have different opinions, the most common belief is that the Canary Islands were actually named after dogs. It was the Romans who first visited these islands, giving them the Latin name
Insulia Canaria

. This translates to "Island of Dogs." Some say that the Romans named the islands for the big dogs they found roaming there. Others believe that the "dogs" on the islands weren't the kinds of dogs we know today. Rather, the animals may have actually been a type of seal, which sailors used to call "sea dogs."

textSplitByBlanks.text: The term
crown shyness

might sound like it describes a timid king or queen. However, it's actually a name for the way some forest trees grow. Strangely, some trees grow in such a way that their tallest branches do not touch the branches of other trees. This means there's a gap between the branches of neighboring trees. Although crown shyness has been studied for many years, scientists are not clear on why it happens. Some think that the trees create gaps to prevent themselves from getting damaged. Others think the gaps are to avoid the spread of harmful insects. The most common belief, however, is that these trees are fighting for light from the sun. Thus, they grow toward the sun and avoid touching other trees that might block their sunlight. The result of crown shyness is a remarkable and beautiful pattern among trees.

So, look up the next time you're in a forest, and you might see this natural wonder.

textSplitByBlanks.text: The saguaro cactus is the largest cactus in the United States. Native to the Sonoran Desert in southern Arizona and western Mexico, the saguaro can grow nearly as tall as a tree. However, this plant grows extremely slowly. At the age of 50, this cactus might still be just a few feet tall. But by the time it's 125 years old, a saguaro may be up to fifty feet tall. Luckily, a saguaro cactus can live up to 200 years.

. A hot spot in the ocean is where magma erupts through Earth's surface on the ocean floor and forms an underwater volcano. Gradually, this process forms islands, like those that make up Hawaii. contents.text: Many paragraphs end with a concluding sentence that lets readers know they've reached the end of the paragraph. A concluding sentence often summarizes the paragraph's topic. A concluding sentence can also tie the ideas in the paragraph together and help the reader connect to them.
Sometimes concluding sentences start with signal words or phrases like In conclusion or To sum up.
For example, maybe your paragraph is about why running is a good form of exercise. Here are two examples of good concluding sentences:

text.text: In short, running is a great way to stay in shape if you don't want to spend money on special equipment or classes.

explanationText.text: This concluding sentence summarizes the topic. It also starts with the signal phrase "In short."

text.text: If you are looking for a cheap, easy way to start exercising, give running a try!

explanationText.text: This concluding sentence ties the ideas in the paragraph together and helps the reader connect to them. It suggests that the reader might want to try running after reading about its benefits.

lessons.name: Use context to identify the meaning of a word

header.text: <instructions>Read the passage and then answer the question.</instructions>

contents.text: In 1492, Christopher Columbus landed on the shores of what came to be called the New World. Other explorers and settlers soon followed Columbus from Europe, many seeking gold and riches. These colonists brought many things with them from Europe, introducing new plants and animals to North America. They also brought several European maladies. The natives of North America had never before been exposed to these strange new diseases. As a result, many became very ill and died. We don't know the full effect that the Europeans had on the native populations. However, many historians believe that up to ninety-five percent of native populations died as a result.
What is the meaning of maladies as used in the passage?

choices.text: sicknesses
guns
fruits and vegetables
machines

contents.text: If you don't know the meaning of a word, you can look for context clues. Context clues are nearby words and phrases that help you figure out the meaning of an unknown word.

header.text: Here are some examples:

sentences.text: Janet's dog punctured her ball with his teeth, causing it to go flat.
You can guess that punctured means "made a hole in."
She had a map, so she offered to be the trip's navigator.
You can guess that a navigator is someone who gives directions on a journey.
The guard closely monitored the building. He was on the lookout for anything that seemed out of place.
You can guess that monitored means "watched."

contents.text: In 1803, the Louisiana Purchase doubled the size of the United States by adding 828,000 square miles of land to the nation. Lewis selected William Clark as second in command. This was the birth of the Lewis and Clark Expedition.

sentences.text: Janet's dog punctured her ball with his teeth, causing it to go flat.
You can guess that punctured means "made a hole in."
She had a map, so she offered to be the trip's navigator.
You can guess that a navigator is someone who gives directions on a journey.
The guard closely monitored the building. He was on the lookout for anything that seemed out of place.
You can guess that monitored means "watched."

contents.text: In 1803, the Louisiana Purchase doubled the size of the United States by adding 828,000 square miles of land to the nation. This acquisition resulted in the U.S. having unexplored territory. So, in 1803, President Thomas Jefferson asked Congress for approval to fund an expedition. The goals of the expedition were to explore the new territory and to find a practical route to the western part of the country. Jefferson chose Meriwether Lewis to lead this expedition. Lewis selected William Clark as second in command. This was the birth of the Lewis and Clark Expedition.
What is the meaning of acquisition as used in the passage?

choices.text: removal
invention
split
addition

content.text: As used in the passage, acquisition means addition.

contents.text: The Industrial Revolution lasted from the 1700s to the mid-1800s. During this time, new machines were invented that changed the way businesses made their products. Some of the machines could spin thread and weave cloth much more quickly than people could. There were machines making other types of products as well. However, the improvements in machines that made fabric created the most new jobs. For this reason, textiles became the dominant industry. People moved to cities in record numbers to work in new factories. The Industrial Revolution changed their lives greatly. In fact, many historians see the Industrial Revolution as one of the most important events in our history.

contents.text: In a lineup of major league baseball players, Pete Gray would be conspicuous. Why? Gray was a baseball player with just one arm. Gray had lost most of his right arm in an accident at age six. Naturally right-handed, he had to learn to do everything with his left hand. This meant that he had to relearn how to throw a ball and swing a bat. Gray was determined to become a professional baseball player, though. He finally got his chance in 1945, when many players were fighting in World War II. Gray played as an outfielder for the St. Louis Browns. People from all over would come to cheer for him when he played. Gray became a role model to many people, including soldiers injured in the war. One of Gray's gloves is now at the Baseball Hall of Fame.
What is the meaning of conspicuous as used in the passage?

choices.text: comfortable
warmed up
easy to notice
one of the shortest

contents.text: Two billion people around the world enjoy eating insects. However, most people in the United States would rather eat dirt than eat a beetle. If you are like most Americans and consider eating insects repugnant, the United Nations would like to change your mind. In 2013, the UN released a report about the benefits of eating bugs. The report says that bugs can be a good source of fiber, protein, vitamins, and minerals. The report suggests that eating bugs can be good for the earth as well. Raising insects for food requires less land and water than raising other animals. Instead of reaching for a hamburger when you're hungry, improve your health and save the earth with a delicious bowl of crickets!
What is the meaning of repugnant as used in the passage?

choices.text: very interesting
extremely disgusting
delightfully different
highly old-fashioned

contents.text: The legend of Molly Pitcher dates from the Revolutionary War. An American gunner named John Hays was at the Battle of Monmouth. Hays's wife, Mary, also known as "Molly," was helping him and the other soldiers. The day was terribly hot. Mary carried a pitcher of water from a nearby spring to the field of battle. The soldiers drank and cooled their cannons with the spring water. "Molly Pitcher" became Mary's new name. She kept bringing more fresh water to the soldiers, replenishing the pitcher again and again. Then, when her husband was unable to continue shooting, Molly took his place at the cannon. She is remembered today as a hero.

contents.text: In the early days of automobiles, rain was a real problem for drivers. Water covered the windshields, so they couldn't see. They had to open their windows and stick their heads outside! When Mary Anderson saw drivers struggling in the rain, she thought she could help. Anderson started working on designs for a rain-clearing device. Even after many failures, she kept experimenting. This persistence resulted in Mary Anderson's invention of the modern windshield wiper. Her design put a rubber blade on a wooden stick. Today's wipers use the same basic principle that Mary Anderson dreamed up in 1903.
What is the meaning of persistence as used in the passage?

the quality of continuing in spite of difficulty
a feeling of sorrow or great sadness

contents.text: The United States court system has three main levels. The first is the District Court, where trials are first held. This trial court's decision is final unless a party appeals to the Court of Appeal. The appeals court considers arguments from both sides and decides who is right. The last level is the United States Supreme Court. The Supreme Court chooses carefully which cases to hear. Those cases usually involve important issues. The Supreme Court may also take a case if something egregious happened in the lower courts. For example, the court might consider a case where someone was denied a fair trial. The Supreme Court hears less than one percent of the cases brought to it.
What is the meaning of egregious as used in the passage?

choices.text: small and easily explained
very bad and easily noticed
new and entertaining
simple to ignore

contents.text: For some tasks, smaller is better. In 2013, two men exploring a South African cave found some bones in an underground chamber. When anthropologist Lee Berger saw photos of the chamber, he thought it was important. But reaching it required squeezing through narrow cave passages, some less than eight inches wide. Berger couldn't fit. He published an ad seeking experienced scientists who could work in caves. Six women met the requirements. These "underground astronauts" dug up more than 1,500 fragments of bones from the cave. From these specimens, Berger's team was able to rebuild fifteen partial skeletons. They concluded that they had discovered a new human ancestor, which they named Homo naledi.
What is the meaning of specimens as used in the passage?

choices.text: small souvenirs
individual pieces
statues or monuments
large granite stones

contents.text: Although plants don't talk, they do communicate with each other by sending messages. For example, scientists have found that some trees can communicate to share resources like water. They do this by sending messages through an underground network. A certain kind of fungus connects all the trees in the forest together, forming a large network. Scientists believe this information-sharing web may allow larger, older trees to help younger trees survive. This improves the health of the entire forest. The details of how the communication works are still obscure, so further research is needed to better understand the process.
